constraints.evidence: Slide 12 bridge: target $98.9M, existing base at today's NRR $94.0M, price +$3.46M, new customers needed $1.46M. States that new-customer bookings are not in the pack and must be reconciled with the 2027 sales plan.

Company NRR 109.3% today and ~113% (base) or 112% (stress) under the plan. 'NRR > 100% holds in every option and case; the binding objective is ARR growth.' SMB NRR 94% is shown as unchanged. No SMB break-even NRR is given, but the headline includes the constraint.
Slide 16: repriceable ARR $65.45M (SMB 100%, MM 85%, Ent 40%). Slide 10 waterfall removes MM ARR not renewing (–0.74) and Ent ARR not renewing (–1.73) before any churn reaction.

Enterprise 60% capped at 7%. Cap effect –$0.29M on the waterfall. Enterprise gross is $0.86M. Slide 14 and the assumptions flag that caps are assumed pro rata (–$0.1M if all renewing Ent ARR is capped).
'$10.3M falls to $7.6M before any churn reaction.' Split SMB 2.52 / MM 4.18 / Ent 0.86. Then $5.3M base and $2.7M stress after churn.

Slide 9 and the appendix model the 2023 response (+0.5pp for 6 months, +0.1pp for 6 months, 3.6% lost for +8%). SMB net is $1.25M at the 2023 response and about $0 at 2×. The headline plan holds SMB prices, so this does not drive the $3.5M. The doc does not explicitly call 2023 a floor, but it does stress it with a doubled response.

Slide 9: Inkwell $9 vs $15, Pro $24 vs Business $29. Gap +67% → +87% after +12%. Win rate 51% → 38%. ~290 lost new SMB wins would erase the $1.25M. Inkwell not seen above 200 seats. SMB is held for this reason, and ≤200-seat MM exposure is a pre-meeting data check.

Slides 4–6 and 17: cohort of 2,100 at ~4.9% vs 2.1%, ~1.0pp of the 1.1pp rise, 52% vs 18% citing price, 41% vs 72% activation, $2,095 vs $4,368 ARR each. The cohort is exempt from any 2027 increase and is treated separately from the $16.6M non-promotion ARR. Its churn is built into SMB NRR of 94%.

Slide 7: customer-weighted 1.7% → 2.6%, ARR-weighted 0.8% → 1.2%, excluding the cohort 1.6% → 1.7%. The board's 1.4% → 2.3% is 'not reproducible'. Decisions are built on segment-level churn, and a defined churn measure is proposed.

Halving needs 1.55%, below the 2.1% non-promotion level. Best case is 2.1% (a 32% cut). Valued at ~$0.4M and 'Do not count it toward 2027 churn targets until H1 results are in'. It is excluded from the headline ARR and NRR. No programme cost is given.

alternatives.evidence: Option C (MM +10%, Ent +10% or 7% capped, SMB held) is the recommendation. It is costed at $3.5M base / $2.4M stress and compared with B and D on ARR, NRR and new-customer need. The differentiation rests on NRR 112–118%, the null 2024 test, and no Inkwell above 200 seats. The doc states it gives up ~$1.8M vs B.

Option B is the CFO's plan correctly costed: $10.3M → $7.6M gross → $5.3M base / $2.7M stress. It is rejected because the SMB part ranges from $1.25M to ~$0, the Inkwell gap widens, and the cohort is fragile.

Move 2 holds SMB and runs a randomised +8% test on new sign-ups, with the promotion cohort exempt and a go/no-go rule at 7% conversion loss. It is valued at $0.3–0.7M. The initial 5–8% SMB hypothesis is also discussed. A uniform 5–7% increase is not costed. The test measures new-sign-up conversion, not renewal churn on the existing base.

Option A (no increase) is costed: $0 added, NRR 109%, $4.9M new-customer ARR needed. Onboarding is evaluated (~$0.4M, cannot halve churn). The lower-priced entry tier against Inkwell is not mentioned.

sensitivities.evidence: SMB +12% is worth $1.25M at the 2023 response and –$0.02M at 2×. Break-even is 10.7% extra loss for +12% and 7.4% for +8% (~2× the 2023 response). The doc gives the ~290 lost new wins that erase the gain and splits promotion from non-promotion on price citing (52% vs 18%). It notes the 2023 response predates Inkwell by stressing at 2×.

MM at SMB-like sensitivity cuts uplift from $3.5M to $2.4M and lifts new-customer need to $2.6M (slide 14, slide 16). MM base is $3.19M vs $2.07M stress at +12%. The doc caveats that the test was on new sign-ups, not renewals, and flags 51–200-seat exposure as a data check. It does not state a break-even MM loss rate, and the stress case is not an explicit flip point.

The cohort decomposition is shown and onboarding is valued at ~$0.4M (churn 4.9% → ~4.1%, best case 2.1%). Slide 14 says 'Upside if it is fading' with no number. The SMB 2027 ARR/NRR baseline is not shown under 'fades' vs 'persists' (SMB NRR stays 94% in both cases). The Jul–Oct 2026 cohort data is flagged as a check.

overclaim.quote: Rising churn comes from the 2025 promotion cohort; the core base has not become more price-sensitive

omissions: The SMB test is on new self-serve sign-ups and measures conversion and win rate. The July go rule and the $0.3–0.7M upside depend on extra churn among existing SMB renewals (~3.6%), which this test cannot measure. The doc does not say how renewal churn would be guarded.
The onboarding programme is recommended ('Fund targeted onboarding') with no cost, budget or payback, only a ~$0.4M ARR benefit built on an assumed 41% → 72% activation.
The lower-priced SMB entry tier against Inkwell is not considered.
unsupported_assumptions: 'MM renewals react like new sign-ups (2.1% extra ARR loss per +10%)': an insignificant 23.1% vs 23.6% conversion gap on new sign-ups is used as the point estimate of renewal ARR loss. This carries most of the $3.5M headline.

'2027 segment NRR equals trailing-12-month NRR (SMB 94%, MM 112%, Ent 118%)': this drives the $94.0M base and the '$1.5M new-customer ARR needed'. It is not backed by evidence, even though MM churn is rising and the cohort is fading.
'Existing customers have switching costs, so they are probably less sensitive, but this is unproven': this is used to justify applying the new-sign-up test to renewals.
'Price response is assumed linear, scaled from +8% / +10% evidence': 0.45pp per 1% from one SMB event is scaled to +12%, and 0.21pp per 1% from one MM test is scaled to renewals.

Onboarding value assumes activation rises from 41% to 72% and non-activated customers churn at exactly 3× the activated rate. The pack says 'about three times' and gives no evidence the cohort can be activated.
Enterprise price response is set to zero in the base case (and +10% on uncapped enterprise is treated as 'evidence-backed') although the 2024 test covered only mid-market new sign-ups.
